A.corrected_claim: All 15 Wendt node names reach runtime as canonicalTerms, but 11 of the 15 (not 10) are composite headings that bundle multiple concepts behind slashes, semicolons, ampersands and parentheticals, and the entry supplies zero aliases on any node (`corpus/index/Wendt - Design for Dasein/_synthesis/book-level-ontology.json` core_nodes carry only concept/gloss/units/centrality/locus; all 15 runtime nodes have `aliases: []`). The pattern is systemic rather than Wendt-specific (306/1722 canonicalTerms corpus-wide are composite; Von Uexkull 34/35, Burke Grammar 36/55, VR Pedagogy 29/60 are worse or comparable), so the fix belongs in the `ontology_format: "header"` template — require an `aliases` line per node and split composite names into atoms. I could not refute the observed fact. Every one of the 10 literal strings the claim quotes exists verbatim in `compiled-index.json` → `canonicalTerms`, and all 10 are node names sourced from the Wendt entry. The mechanism the claim relies on also checks out, and the location it cites is exactly right (compile-corpus-index.py:102 literally says "nodes in _synthesis/book-level-ontology.md §3A"; Wendt is registered at compile-corpus-index.py:128-132 with `ontology_format: "header"`).

WHAT IS CONFIRMED
- Exactly 15 ontologyNodes carry `"text": "Wendt - Design for Dasein"` — the denominator is right (counted from compiled-index.json, no .backups paths involved).
- All 15 names land in canonicalTerms; I resolved each to a line number (e.g. compiled-index.json:15325 'embodied philosophy / phenomenological design thinking'; :15334 'ready-to-hand / present-at-hand continuum + breakdown'; :15323 'multistability & creative misuse; intention not primary'; :15368 'technē / poiēsis / standing reserve / enframing'; :15527 "thing / gathering (the jug's void)"; :15463 'craft vs design; the hand; un-throwing'; :15474 'sense vs meaning; meaning over utility'; :15505 'design as being-in-the-world / care'; :15620 'transparency, not invisibility'; :15795 'affordance + embodiment'). Not off-by-one, not blank lines.
- The Wendt entry supplies ZERO aliases at every layer — `core_nodes` in `_synthesis/book-level-ontology.json` has only keys {centrality, concept, gloss, locus, units}; `grep -i alias` on that file returns nothing; all 15 runtime nodes have `"aliases": []`. So there is no fallback handle. This is the aggravating fact the claim did not state and it makes the claim stronger, not weaker.
- The runtime consumer is real and is defeated: smart-retrieval-layer.ts:268-270 filters `canonicalTerms.filter(t => t.length >= 4 && queryLower.includes(t.toLowerCase()))` — the FULL phrase must be a substring of the query for the +0.10 CANONICAL_BOOST (line 273) to fire. A second consumer is defeated the same way: corpus-index-provider.ts:177-182 `expandQueryWithOntology` requires a `\b<full name>\b` regex hit against the query. Neither will ever fire for a 54-character slash-and-semicolon phrase.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRONG (why I am correcting rather than affirming as-is)
1. Category "unreachable-content" is wrong, and the consequence overreaches. The Wendt nodes ARE reachable at runtime by a third path the claim did not check: corpus-index-provider.ts:107-118 `loadCorpusIndexContext` splits the topic into individual ≥4-char words and scores them with `scoreCandidate` against a concatenation of name + greek + transliteration + DEFINITION + aliases. A topic containing "affordance" or "embodiment" or "breakdown" scores these nodes fine and emits them as ontologyLines. The entry's content is degraded in term matching, not unreachable.
2. "Effectively 5 usable terms out of 15" is the wrong residual, and generous in the wrong direction. The 5 survivors are 'anti-Cartesianism' (:16089), 'mediation as constitutive' (:15747), "Ihde's four mediation relations" (:15587), 'problem-solution paradox' (:15782), and 'abduction / design thinking (4 parts)' (:15476) — the last is just as composite (slash + parenthetical) as the 10 flagged. Real residual is 4 of 15 names, i.e. the claim understates. Offsetting that, the entry actually contributes 17 canonicalTerms, not 15: the `greek` field was misused as a gloss slot on two nodes, leaking "the jug's void" (:16298) and '4 parts' (:16713) into canonicalTerms via build_canonical_terms's `greek` harvest at compile-corpus-index.py:1284-1288. '4 parts' at length 7 clears the `length >= 4` gate and is a false-positive magnet, which is a separate small defect the claim missed.

"build_canonical_terms() sorts by length descending 'for greedy matching'" is a true quote (compile-corpus-index.py:11-12, 1281, 1303-1304) but is causally irrelevant: the runtime does `.filter(...).some(...)`, never a longest-match scan, so sort order changes nothing. The claim's conclusion survives on the substring check alone, but its stated basis is not the operative one.
4. It is presented as a Wendt-specific defect; it is a corpus-wide authoring/compiler pattern. Composite names by entry: Von Uexkull 34/35, Burke Grammar 36/55, VR Pedagogy 29/60, Calleja 27/44, Gross 25/36, Aristotle Metaphysics 11/12 — against Wendt's 10/15. Wendt is a representative instance of a systemic `ontology_format: "header"` problem, not an outlier. That does not make it a design decision to be excused, but it does mean the fix is at the compiler/template level and the per-entry severity is not HIGH.

AGAINST THE USER'S CLAUSE-LEVEL GOAL, the finding is real and worth keeping: node 13 'technē / poiēsis / standing reserve / enframing' bundles four distinct concepts into a single index atom, and node 15 bundles three. That is movement in the opposite direction from claim/clause granularity — the entry is not merely un-matchable, it is structurally coarser than the chapter-level unit it already sits at.

A.claim: manifest declares synthesis_files: 22; the _synthesis directory contains 24 files.
A.corrected_claim: No count mismatch. `synthesis_files: 22` and the gate row "Synthesis deliverables | ~22 (phantasia-cluster parity) | 22 | ✓" both count synthesis DELIVERABLES, which correctly excludes the two bookkeeping artifacts (`manifest.json`, `quality-gates-report.md`). The `_synthesis` directory holds 24 raw files, of which exactly 22 are deliverables. The declared parity baseline confirms the denominator: the model cluster `Aristotelian Phantasia Secondary (1985-2017)/_synthesis` contains exactly 22 files and contains NO manifest.json and NO quality-gates-report.md anywhere in the entry — so "phantasia-cluster parity = 22" is by construction a count of deliverables only, and RDR2's 22 is an exact apples-to-apples match. At most, the word "files" in the manifest.status prose (manifest.json:35, "_synthesis (22 files, ...)") is loose wording for the same deliverable count; that is a cosmetic phrasing nit, not a falsely-passing gate.
A.reasoning:
The finding trips two of the listed failure modes at once — wrong denominator, and mistaking a design decision for a defect.

The reporting agent compared a raw `ls` count (24 directory entries) against a metric that is explicitly named "Synthesis **deliverables**" and explicitly scoped by "(phantasia-cluster parity)". Those two qualifiers define the denominator, and I tested both. `manifest.json` is the record making the assertion — a set that counts itself is the anomaly, not the exclusion. `quality-gates-report.md` is the gate report itself, and it postdates the manifest by 79 minutes, so it could not have been in scope when `synthesis_files: 22` was written.

The parity baseline is the decisive evidence, because it is falsifiable and it held: the phantasia cluster's `_synthesis` contains exactly 22 files, and I verified by find that the entire phantasia entry contains no `manifest.json` and no `quality-gates-report.md` at any depth. Its 22 is therefore a pure deliverables count. RDR2 declaring 22 against that baseline is correct and self-consistent; had RDR2 declared 24 it would have been the one out of parity, overstating its output by counting two bookkeeping files the model cluster does not even produce.

The stated consequence also does not follow. "A declared count that a gate table marks PASS is wrong by 2" requires the gate to be measuring raw files; it is measuring deliverables, and it passes truthfully. The propagation concern is likewise empty — grep shows the number appears in exactly three places, all internal to `_synthesis`, and the entry's own gates report documents that this cluster is intentionally outside `compiled-index.json`, so no consumer ingests the figure.

The one residue worth recording, and it is cosmetic: `manifest.json:35` writes the status prose as "_synthesis (22 files, ...)" where "deliverables" would be strictly accurate. That is imprecise wording of a correct count, not a false gate, and does not support HIGH, or any, severity.

Worth flagging against the user's ultimate goal, since it reframes what this metric is worth: even fully correct, `synthesis_files` is a file-cardinality gate. It certifies that 22 artifacts exist; it certifies nothing about whether their contents are complete, current, or mutually consistent. A cluster could pass this gate with 22 empty files. Counting-based gates of this kind are structurally incapable of supporting a claim-level or clause-level index — they measure the container, never the claims inside it. Auditing effort on this entry is better spent on the content-bearing counts (the 506 global edges, the 65 lemmas) than on file tallies.

A.entry: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
A.path_line: corpus/index/Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans/uex-analysis/book-level-ontology.md (§3A) vs tension-edges.json vs concept-matrix.csv vs global-edges.csv vs phase0-overview.md
A.claim: Four mutually incompatible German orthographies coexist inside one entry, and the corrupted one is the one that reaches runtime.
A.corrected_claim:
CONFIRMED, and worse than stated in two respects; two supporting details are wrong.

CORE CLAIM — CONFIRMED. Four mutually incompatible German orthographies coexist in this entry, and the runtime-reachable layer is corrupt.

The compiler reads exactly two files from this entry (scripts/compile-corpus-index.py:1219-1226 book-level-ontology.md; :1267-1269 tension-edges.json). BOTH are corrupt, in DIFFERENT dialects — the claim understates this by saying "the corrupted one" (singular):
  - book-level-ontology.md §3A (line 9; rows :20 Gegengefuge, :22 Bedeutungstrager, :24 Planmassigkeit, :27 Wohnhulle, :29 "Ton / Tonung") = full ASCII fold. grep -o 'ü' → 0.
  - tension-edges.json (:12 Planmaessigkeit, :20 Bedeutungstraeger, :53 Kausalitaet) = ae/ue digraph.
The two correct-orthography files reach runtime through NOTHING: global-edges.csv (:7 Gegengefüge, :31 Planmäßigkeit, :57 Einprägung, :59 Tönung, :69 Bedeutungsträger, :82 Wohnhülle, :99 Kausalität) is touched only by the manual CLI scripts/normalize-edges.py:40, which writes to stdout; uex-german-appendix.json holds the ground-truth register of 19 correctly-spelled compounds and is read by no code at all.

CONSEQUENCE — CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY, not merely asserted. src/god-agent/universal/corpus-index-provider.ts:80-89 scores candidates with `new RegExp(...,'gi')` over `.toLowerCase()` — no NFD/NFKD, no umlaut folding, anywhere in the retrieval path. Replaying that scorer against the shipped corpus/index/compiled-index.json: 'Gegengefüge' → [], 'Bedeutungsträger' → [], 'Planmäßigkeit' → [], 'Wohnhülle' → []; only the corrupt spelling 'Gegengefuge' returns a hit. A drafting query in correct German silently returns zero.

WORSE THAN STATED (1): the claim lists 4 corrupted runtime node names; there are 5. book-level-ontology.md:29 publishes "Ton / Tonung", where correct German is Tönung (global-edges.csv:59; uex-german-appendix.json:1334). Of the 35 compiled uex ontology nodes, exactly 5 node names should carry ä/ö/ü/ß, and 5 of 5 are corrupt — 100% of the affected population, not 4/35.

WORSE THAN STATED (2): the two runtime layers do not join to each other. Of 18 distinct tension-edge node ids, 11 fail to resolve against any ontology node name; 2 of those (Bedeutungstraeger, Planmaessigkeit) fail PURELY on orthography — the concept exists as a node under Bedeutungstrager / Planmassigkeit. So the corruption severs the node↔tension join inside the compiled artifact itself.

EVIDENCE ERRORS in the original finding (both minor, neither refuting):
  1. "phase0-overview.md and all 14 phase2-*.md → correct" is FALSE. phase2-uex-m1.md is in the digraph dialect: 20× Bedeutungstraeger, 4× Wohnhuelle, 1× Gegengefuege (e.g. :10, :25, :64-67). It is 13 of 14, not 14. That file even mixes dialects in one table cell — :73 "Buehne / Lebensbühne".
  2. The count "four" is right for the entry but its stated basis is wrong: the four probed files span only THREE dialects, because tension-edges.json and concept-matrix.csv are the SAME dialect (ae/ue digraph). The genuine fourth dialect is in uex-german-appendix.md — umlaut stripped but ß retained — which contradicts itself in a single line, :748 "**Forms encountered**: Plan, Planmaßigkeit, Planmassigkeit", and never records the correct Planmäßigkeit. The file whose sole job is the German lemma register is itself corrupt (grep -o 'ü' → 0, ß → 9).

NOT A DESIGN DECISION: grep -rni 'umlaut|ascii|orthograph|transliterat|encoding|normali' over the whole entry returns zero hits — no convention is documented. And the compiled nodes carry `"aliases": []` for all 35 uex nodes, so no correct-spelling alias exists to recover the match. This is unintentional corruption, not an ASCII-safe-ID scheme.

SEVERITY corrected CRITICAL → HIGH (top of band). Downgrade rationale: no information is lost — uex-german-appendix.json and global-edges.csv hold the correct orthography on disk, so the fix is a mechanical rewrite of two files plus a recompile; and the blast radius is bounded to 5 node names and 3 tension node ids inside 1 of 27 entries. Retained at HIGH rather than MEDIUM because the failure is total on the affected population (5/5), entirely silent, present in the shipped runtime artifact, and invisible to every existing check.

AGAINST THE USER'S CLAUSE-LEVEL GOAL: this is the diagnostic case. In a claim/clause-level index the German lemma IS the join key across layers. This entry demonstrates that the pipeline has no lemma-identity discipline whatsoever — four spellings, no normalization at write time, no folding at read time, no alias bridge, and the one file designated as the terminology register disagreeing with itself. Fixing the Uexküll spellings would repair this entry while leaving the structural defect intact; the entry is excellent by its own template (35 nodes, 14 units, source PDF present and stat-verified at corpus/rhetorical_ontology/von Uexkull, Jacob - ...[Clean Copy].pdf, 197MB) yet structurally incapable of the claim-level target until lemma identity is enforced at compile time.
A.reasoning:
I attempted to refute and could not. Every probe reproduced the claimed bytes, and the consequence — which is the part audits most often get wrong — held up under direct simulation of the runtime scorer rather than assertion.

Ruled out each of the named failure modes: line numbers are correct and land on content lines (§3A header at :9, table rows at :20/:22/:24/:27); no .backups/ paths were counted (all probes scoped to uex-analysis/, and the two compiled-index consumers under .backups/ and tmp/ were explicitly excluded when locating the live provider); the denominator is right once restated as 5-of-5 umlaut-bearing node names rather than 4-of-35 nodes; the "missing" correct-orthography data does exist under other names (uex-german-appendix.json, global-edges.csv) but reaches runtime through nothing, which supports rather than refutes the claim; and it is not a design decision, since no orthography convention is documented anywhere in the entry and the compiled nodes carry empty alias arrays that would otherwise recover the match.

Two supporting details in the evidence are genuinely wrong — phase2-uex-m1.md is in the digraph dialect (so 13 of 14 phase2 files are clean, not 14), and the four probed exemplar files span only three dialects because tension-edges.json and concept-matrix.csv share the ae/ue form. The stated count of four is nonetheless correct for the entry, because a fourth dialect the claim never identified as such exists in uex-german-appendix.md. This is the "count is right but its stated basis is wrong" pattern, so I corrected the basis rather than the number.

I also found the entry is worse than reported: Tönung is a fifth corrupted runtime node name, both compiler-visible files are corrupt in different dialects rather than one, and the corruption severs the node-to-tension join inside the compiled artifact itself.

Severity moved CRITICAL to HIGH on calibration, not on doubt. The corruption is total and silent on its population and ships in the runtime artifact, but the correct spellings survive on disk in two files, so nothing is unrecoverable and the repair is mechanical. I reserve CRITICAL for unrecoverable loss or system-wide breakage; this is bounded to one entry. The parent should override upward if entry-scoped retrieval misses on dissertation-critical terminology are treated as CRITICAL in this audit's rubric.

C.true_cause:
The plan is NOT blameless; it is the proximate cause. But the mechanism is a mis-routing instruction plus a mis-measuring gate, not an omission. Three contributing layers, in order of blame:

1. PLAN (primary): :142 routed load-bearing edges into `_synthesis/manifest.json`, a file with no reader. §2.4 (:158-168) then described the relations semantically with no schema and no reader trace, while :154-156 shows the author DID trace the compiler for nodes. §2.6.4's gate measured node counts only, so the loss was undetectable at sign-off. §1.4's gate demanded an impossible −24 edge delta from a CSV the compiler never opens.

2. COMPILER (contributing, not exculpating): `parse_tension_edges`/`_normalize_tension_edge` drop malformed or foreign-schema edges silently (`return None`, compile-corpus-index.py:1130), and `collect_tension_edges` (L1252-1271) emits no warning when a registered TEXT_DIRS entry has no `tension-edges.json` at all — it just `continue`s past the missing file. Only the ONTOLOGY collector warns on a missing file ("Ontology file not found", L1227). So an entry can register successfully, pass every gate, and contribute zero edges with no diagnostic anywhere. A plan cannot be blamed for the silence, but a plan CAN be blamed for shipping a gate that relies on that silence.

3. EXECUTING AGENT (minimal): the author deviated from the plan only in adding a third outbound relation (`derives-to → vle-02`, manifest.json:36) beyond the two §2.4 mandated, and in omitting the optional construct-correspondences exactly as §2.4's default directed. The agent followed :142 verbatim. No deviation explains the defect.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (independently, via a different code path than the one cited). For `*rel{k, ...}, k = $p` as the FIRST atom in a rule body, Cozo 0.7.13-alpha.3 does execute a full relation scan with a post-filter. The actual 14-step chain:
1. compile.rs:171 — every rule body starts `ret = RelAlgebra::unit(...)`.
2. compile.rs:250-268 — at the Relation atom, `k` is not yet in `seen_variables`, so it is `IndexPositionUse::BindForLater`, not `Join`.
3. compile.rs:270-284 — `store.choose_index(...)` returns `None` (relation.rs:201-203: `if self.indices.is_empty() { return None }`), so a plain `RelAlgebra::Stored` is built.
4. ra.rs:653-670 — `RelAlgebra::join` UNCONDITIONALLY wraps into `RelAlgebra::Join(InnerJoin{left: unit, right: Stored})`. There is no `is_unit()` collapse. (The `is_unit()` at ra.rs:311 is inside `impl Debug for RelAlgebra` — it hides the unit join in PRINTED plans only, which is likely how the claim's author was misled about which node executes.)
5. compile.rs:601-626 — `k = $p` hits `seen_variables.contains(&u.binding)` → `ret.filter(build_equate(...))`. (This part of the claim is exactly right.)
6. ra.rs:552-595 — the `RelAlgebra::Join` arm of `filter` pushes the predicate DOWN into `right` because its bindings are a subset of the right bindings.
7. ra.rs:518-533 — the `Stored` arm appends it to `StoredRA.filters`.
8. ra.rs:2170-2188 — `InnerJoin::iter`, `Stored` arm, computes `join_indices` = `([], [])`.
9. ra.rs:1512-1520 — `join_is_prefix(&[])`: `l = 0`, `[].into_iter().eq(0..0)` → TRUE. So it calls `prefix_join`, NOT `iter()`.
10. ra.rs:1322-1333 — `left_to_prefix_indices.len()` (0) `>= key_len` (>=1) is false → not `point_lookup_join`.
11. ra.rs:1345-1351 — `compute_bounds(&self.filters, other_bindings)` IS CALLED, with the pushed-down equality filter.
12. data/expr.rs:522-604 — **`extract_bound` has arms only for `OP_GE`/`OP_GT`, `OP_LE`/`OP_LT`, `OP_STARTS_WITH`, and `_ => ValueRange::default()`. There is NO `OP_EQ` arm** (grep for `OP_EQ` in lines 522-606 returns 0). `build_equate` emits `op: &OP_EQ` (data/expr.rs:295-301). So every bound comes back `{lower: Null, upper: Bot}`.
13. ra.rs:1352-1354 — `!l_bound.all(==Null) || !u_bound.all(==Bot)` → `false || false` → the bounded branch is skipped; `skip_range_check = true`.
14. ra.rs:1374-1388 → `scan_prefix(tx, &[])`, then `eval_bytecode_pred` per row. relation.rs:428-443 confirms empty prefix = whole-relation range scan.

D.claim: The artifact is perfectly uniform: exactly one key order per record type across all 837 records, all scalars are strings, no nulls, no missing keys, units/aliases always list[str]. This makes a byte-identical Rust emitter tractable.
D.corrected_claim: The artifact's three keyed record types are uniform — exactly one key order each across 837 records, all scalars strings, no nulls, no missing keys, units/aliases always list[str] — and this holds on both the live artifact and the committed HEAD version. However, that covers only 33% of the artifact's 2,559 records; canonicalTerms (1,722 records, 67%) is a list of bare strings and was not audited. A BYTE-IDENTICAL Rust emitter is NOT tractable, and is impossible even for the incumbent against itself, for two reasons: builtAt is a microsecond wall-clock timestamp (compile-corpus-index.py:1375), and 202 canonicalTerms sit in 101 tie groups whose emitted order is decided by hash-randomized CPython set iteration (:1283 -> :1304) — 8 runs produced 8 different orderings, and 48 of the 101 groups are demonstrably ordered differently across three real compiles in git history. What IS tractable is a FUNCTIONALLY equivalent Rust emitter validated by a normalized comparison (drop builtAt, impose a total tie-break), since the formatting mechanics map cleanly onto serde_json's default 2-space pretty printer with raw UTF-8, and the tie nondeterminism is semantically inert for archon's consumer, which lowercases both query and term before lookup (index.rs:347/354). Two caveats for the port: Python's -len(t) is codepoints where Rust str::len() is bytes (143 terms contain Greek; archon-evidence/src/index.rs:319 already handles this correctly via chars().count()), and the uniformity is unenforced — four hand-maintained duplicate dict literals at :379/:495/:663/:756 with no normalizer, schema, or validator — so it is a snapshot property, not an invariant.
D.reasoning:
The claim's three key-order facts are TRUE — I reproduced them independently, and additionally on the committed HEAD version (a second, different generation of the artifact: 670 nodes / 1,663 terms vs live 701 / 1,722). Same key orders, same key sets, all scalars str, no nulls, no missing keys, units/aliases always list[str]. So the factual half is confirmed and I am not disputing it.

The load-bearing half — "This makes a byte-identical Rust emitter tractable" — is refuted on three independent grounds, and the offered evidence never touches any of them.

(1) SCOPE HOLE: the evidence audits 837 records, but the artifact has 2,559. `canonicalTerms` is 1,722 records — 67% of the artifact — and was excluded from the uniformity audit because it is a list of bare strings with no keys to order. That excluded 67% is exactly where byte-identity fails.

(2) BYTE-IDENTITY IS IMPOSSIBLE EVEN PYTHON-vs-PYTHON. scripts/compile-corpus-index.py:1375 emits `"builtAt": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()` — microsecond precision. Live value: "2026-07-29T19:08:35.589629+00:00". Two consecutive runs of the incumbent itself never produce identical bytes.

(3) ORDERING IS NON-DETERMINISTIC ACROSS RUNS. compile-corpus-index.py:1283 builds `terms: set[str] = set()`; :1304 returns `sorted(terms, key=lambda t: (-len(t), t.lower()))`. Python's sort is stable, so tied elements keep their input order — which is CPython set-iteration order, randomized by per-process string hashing. I measured 101 tie groups (202 members) where two terms share both length and `.lower()` (they differ only in case: 'Care'/'care', 'Time'/'time', 'Historicality'/'historicality'). Probe: 8 default-seed runs produced 8 DISTINCT order fingerprints. This is not theoretical — FIELD EVIDENCE from git history: comparing live vs HEAD vs HEAD~1 (three real historical compiles), 48 of the 101 tie groups are ordered differently. There is therefore no fixed byte target to be identical to.

The correct acceptance criterion is a NORMALIZED comparison (drop builtAt, impose a total tie-break on canonicalTerms), not byte equality. That matters practically: the rhetorical value of "byte-identical" was that port correctness could be proven with a cheap `diff`. It cannot. A normalizing comparator has to be built, and it is itself a place bugs hide.

WHAT SURVIVES (the claim is weakened, not inverted). Formatting mechanics genuinely are reproducible: :1385 uses `json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"`; the file carries 14,482 non-ASCII bytes and ZERO `\uXXXX` escapes (33 literal U+2194, Greek throughout), which serde_json's default 2-space pretty formatter matches natively. And the nondeterminism is semantically INERT for archon's consumer: archon-cli/crates/archon-evidence/src/index.rs:347 lowercases the query, :354 lowercases each term, and keys `term_to_nodes` by the lowercased form, so case-only tied variants collapse to the same lookup; :319 `sort_by_key(Reverse(s.chars().count()))` is stable and already uses codepoints. So a FUNCTIONALLY equivalent Rust emitter is tractable — a BYTE-IDENTICAL one is not, and does not need to be.

TWO PORT GOTCHAS THE CLAIM'S FRAMING HIDES. (a) `-len(t)` is Unicode CODEPOINTS; Rust `str::len()` is BYTES. 143 canonicalTerms contain Greek, so a naive `.len()` port reorders them wholesale (archon already gets this right at index.rs:319). (b) Uniformity is NOT enforced anywhere — it is four hand-maintained duplicate dict literals at compile-corpus-index.py:379, :495, :663, :756, all coincidentally in the same order, with no shared constructor, no schema file, no validator. "Exactly one key order" is an emergent snapshot property that a sixth parser breaks silently. It did hold across two generations, so it is not fragile in practice today, but it is not an invariant a Rust emitter can rely on.

HAZARD CHECKED AND CLEARED (reporting for completeness): Python `str.lower()` and Rust `to_lowercase()` both apply the Greek final-sigma rule, a classic sort-key divergence. Zero terms contain capital sigma, so it does not apply here.

Verdict: refuted as stated. The evidence is correct but does not support the conclusion drawn from it, because it examined only the 33% of records where uniformity is trivially true and never examined the timestamp, record ordering, or the 67% where reproducibility actually breaks.

The doc comment at quote_verify.rs:341 says "Sentence-tight bbox"; that is false. sub_span_bbox unions whole Marker blocks overlapping the span, so the box is as tall as the enclosing paragraph. D. Bekker precision is page-level, off by up to ~30 lines. The quote is at 431b21 — the pdftotext line map shows the margin line-marker "20" at y=329.5, immediately beside the quote's first line. Archon reports 431b1, the first anchor on the page. quote_verify.rs:436-439 explicitly ranks LineNumber at 0 and defers "the determinacy-aware Bekker→page fallback" to "a later phase". The safety valve is permanently closed at current corpus size and gets worse with growth. `docs search "eye-tracking fixation"` succeeds (hybrid mode), so the defect is specific to the verify-quote path the claim rests on.
